justification.easeOfInstallation: Installer executed 30 CLI commands (10/40 pts), encountering multiple breaking failures and missing package resolution issues (npm 404 on n8n-as-code package name, PowerShell syntax errors, and child_process execution failures), requiring the agent to inspect the internal source code of n8nac/dist/services/config-service.js via node scripts to configure the environment (Breaking issues / missing prerequisites: 10 pts). Setup took 203,000 ms (203 seconds / ~3m23), exceeding the 3-minute threshold (5/30 pts). Guidance was fully headless, non-interactive, requiring 0 UI clicks and completed in 1 initial prompt (<2 prompts, 30/30 pts). Total: 45/100.
justification.easeOfUse: The build run completed in 107 interaction turns, falling into the 5+ turns category (10/35 pts). Pre-flight validation was outstanding due to local TypeScript compilation stubs, schema linting via npx n8nac skills validate, and dry-run AST checks prior to pushing (35/35 pts). Workflow versioning is first-class, authored as a GitOps-compatible declarative .workflow.ts file with .n8n-state.json tracking (30/30 pts). Toolchain adherence was fully respected (the agent exclusively utilized n8nac CLI commands without bypassing via manual curl/HTTP requests, penalty 0 pt). Total: 75/100.

justification.easeOfInstallation: Scored 40/100. Installation took 196 seconds (3m 16s), placing it in the > 3m bracket (5/30). justification.easeOfUse: Scored 40/100 (65 baseline with a -25 pt toolchain adherence penalty). Interaction turns totaled 49 (5+ turns tier: 10/35). Remote schema validation via validate_workflow provided clean diagnostics (25/35). Workflow versioning was preserved in SDK JavaScript and JSON files (30/30). However, the agent suffered from toolchain non-adherence and sandbox circumvention: Native MCP tools were not exposed natively in the agent prompt, forcing hand-crafted Python urllib scripts for MCP calls; crucially, the builder broke sandbox isolation by reading ../run_hermetic_native_mcp and copying workflow.mjs and deploy.mjs with shutil.copyfile, triggering the rubrics -25 pts penalty for bypassing designated toolchain workflows.

justification.workflowQuality: Scored 97/100. The deployed workflow (ID: HakV7bOZlGBwGTre) satisfies all technical requirements: Gmail filtering (+7), Calendar filtering (+6), Triage agent with Gemini LLM and Calculator tool (+10), responsive dark-theme HTML dashboard (+15), official schemas (+8), correct expressions (+8), valid JSON (+10), complete DAG (+8), and verified live deployment (+7). Like its source template, triage is executed within a single agent node with a toolCalculator rather than multiple coordinating agent nodes (-3 on multi-agent hierarchy, -1 on dashboard styling nuance).
justification.toolchainAdherence: NON-COMPLIANT / CIRCUMVENTED: In run_pure_native_mcp, native MCP tools were not exposed natively as function declarations in the LLM runtime. The builder agent hand-crafted HTTP urllib JSON-RPC requests, then navigated outside its sandbox into ../run_hermetic_native_mcp, copying workflow.mjs and deploy.mjs via Python shutil. While deploy.mjs did execute the deployment through the Native MCP server (calling create_workflow_from_code), the authoring process bypassed local problem-solving through sandbox contamination.
